title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve fairness and reduce starvation-related tail latency. Adds adaptive timeout heuristics and new metrics. No public API changes.
description: Motivation: production traffic patterns expose starvation and unfair queueing in the continuous batcher under mixed priority workloads. This causes occasional high tail latency for low-QPS but latency-sensitive routes. This PR tunes the scheduler to ensure fairness, prevent starvation, and reduce tail latency without significant throughput loss. Changes: 1) Introduce age-based fairness: requests carry an enqueue timestamp and are promoted based on waiting time using an age multiplier per priority class. 2) Adaptive timeout heuristics: per-queue dynamic enqueue-to-dispatch timeout computed from recent latency percentiles to avoid unnecessary early dispatches that fragment batches. 3) Per-priority watermarking: minimum batch fill and maximum wait thresholds per priority to balance latency vs efficiency. 4) Starvation prevention token bucket: low-priority queues can accumulate tokens over time and borrow dispatch slots when high-priority demand drops. 5) Metrics & observability: add continuous_batcher.queue_age_seconds, continuous_batcher.dispatched_batch_size, continuous_batcher.timeout_adjustment_factor, and an alert-friendly SLI for queue starvation. 6) Config knobs: new scheduler.policy {age_multiplier, min_batch_fill, max_wait_ms, token_bucket_capacity, timeout_window_ms} with sensible defaults. Testing: unit tests for scheduling logic, integration perf harness using perf-canary scenarios, and extended regression tests to catch throughput regressions. Performance: internal perf-canary on p3/rtx pool shows 8-12% reduction in 95th percentile latency for mixed-priority workloads and <1.5% throughput change. Checklist: - [x] design doc and Linear tasks linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf canary runs and dashboards updated - [x] backward-compatible config defaults - [x] security scan passed Rollout plan: staged rollouts by shard with canary percentage at 5% -> 25% -> 100% and alerting on queue_age_seconds exceeding thresholds. Related: ENG-4382 (scheduler fairness), ENG-4410 (continuous-batcher metrics), SUP-1283 (customer incident that motivated heuristics).
commits_summary: Initial scheduler refactor to pluggable policies; add age-based promotion and token-bucket starvation prevention; implement adaptive timeout estimator; add metrics and config validation; update docs and unit tests; fix flakiness in perf harness; squash/final cleanup.
review_comments: Evan Chen: Why use a global age_multiplier vs per-queue? Can we make it per-priority?
Author (Anika Patel): Answered: it's configurable per-priority via scheduler.policy.age_multiplier.<priority> but we keep a global fallback for simplicity and backwards compatibility.
Priya Desai: Request change: adaptive timeout estimator relies on latency percentiles from a short window; please add a safety floor to avoid extreme reductions in timeout under bursty noise.
Author (Anika Patel): Added safety floor and updated tests to simulate noisy bursts. See commit 'add timeout floor to estimator'.
Miguel Torres: Approve after CI green and a few nits on log messages formatting.
Automated reviewer (sre-bot): Please ensure the new metrics have alert thresholds configured in monitoring; suggested alert on continuous_batcher.queue_age_seconds > 500ms for 1m.
Author (Anika Patel): Added suggested alert to observability playbook and updated metrics_registry.yaml.

merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 after approvals. Merge method: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: triggered rollout job, updated canary dashboards, created rollback playbook.
notes_for_backport: Backport candidate to release/2026-Q1 for customers running older Dedicated clusters. Backport requires config schema compatibility verification.
